Subject: TLS termination for private endpoints — what do you recommend?

Hi Soojin / Markus,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood Private last week. We're starting to map the network and cert ownership for the deployment into our VPC. A few constraints on our side:
- All external-facing hostnames must resolve only inside our VPC (split-horizon DNS).
- We manage certificates with HashiCorp Vault (private CA). Let's Encrypt is not an option.
- Audit trail and key custody are strict: cert private keys should live in our HSM when possible.
- We prefer mutual TLS for control-plane APIs, optional for data-plane.

Two implementation questions for the architecture review:
1) Do you recommend terminating TLS at our ALB (customer-side) and proxying plain HTTP to Redwood, or terminating inside the Redwood stack (in our VPC) and keeping TLS end-to-end?
2) If Redwood manages cert rotation, can you integrate with our Vault/HSM? Or do you require us to supply certs?

I've attached an initial network diagram and our Vault cert policy for context. Can we get a short proposal (2–3 options) and recommended tradeoffs?

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Corporation

Attachments: tls-diagram-v2.png, vault-cert-policy.docx
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: TLS termination for private endpoints — what do you recommend?

Alice — thanks for the detail and the diagrams, those are helpful. High-level recommendations (short list so we can pick):

Option A — Customer-edge TLS termination (ALB/NGW)
- Terminate TLS at Acme ALB using certificates issued by your Vault (private CA).
- ALB does TLS offload and forwards to Redwood Private instances over an internal encrypted network (we recommend mTLS between ALB and Redwood ingress).
- Pros: you retain key custody in your HSM; simpler for compliance.
- Cons: limited visibility into TLS metrics on Redwood side; requires ALB config for SNI routing if multiple hostnames.

Option B — Redwood-managed termination inside VPC (TLS to Redwood ingress)
- Redwood terminates TLS inside the private deployment; certs are either (1) supplied by you and stored in your KMS with an API integration, or (2) Redwood manages short-lived certs but private keys are generated ephemeral and wrapped by your KMS/HSM.
- Pros: better observability, easier to support advanced features (payload inspection, structured logging), and simpler wildcard/SAN handling.
- Cons: you must permit Redwood to access cert material via an integration; increases audit scope.

Option C — TLS passthrough + mTLS at app layer
- ALB does TCP pass-through; backend handles TLS and mTLS termination at app. Good if you require end-to-end mTLS initiated by clients.
- Pros: strict end-to-end encryption and fine-grained client auth.
- Cons: more complex for routing and ALB health checks.

Operational notes / recommended guardrails:
- DNS: use a private hosted zone (Route53/Cloud DNS) authored by your infra team. Redwood will provide canonical CNAMEs for services (e.g. rdp-acme-prod.redwood-internal) so you can point private hostnames to the right service.
- Cert rotation: we can integrate with Vault via our connector (read-only cert request flow) or accept PEM bundles you upload to a customer-kept bucket. We support ACME but only for public CAs — not applicable here.
- Audit: we can emit key rotation and cert-presented telemetry into your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch.
- mTLS: Redwood supports client cert validation; we can enforce against your CA chain.

Next steps: can you confirm whether Acme prefers ALB termination (Option A) or Redwood-managed (Option B)? If Option B, we'll need:
- Vault PKI API endpoint & an integration user (scoped to issue/renew certificates), or
- A key-wrap policy that allows us to create ephemeral keys and have you wrap them in your HSM.

Happy to sketch configuration snippets (ALB listeners, SNI rules, Terraform) once we have the choice. Can we schedule a 30m follow-up?

— Soojin

Subject: Re: TLS termination for private endpoints — DNS and SAN considerations

Following Soojin's note, a few concrete DNS / cert engineering points to avoid surprises: 

- Split-horizon / private zone: create a private hosted zone named acme.internal (or the hostnames you want) and add A/CNAMEs that point to the internal LB that fronts Redwood. We recommend CNAMEs from customer-visible hostnames to canonical Redwood hostnames (rdp-<env>.redwood-internal).
- SANs vs wildcard: prefer SAN lists over wide wildcards for least privilege. Wildcards are convenient but cause problems for multi-tenant DNS and subject validation in certs.
- TTL and failover: keep TTLs low (60–300s) during rollout so you can reroute quickly.
- Health checks & ALB: if you terminate at ALB (Option A), configure L7 health checks using a short path (/healthz?signed=...) that presents a signed token so backends can validate origin.
- Validation: for cert CN/SAN validation we will verify the leaf cert chain against your CA. If you want us to generate CSRs, include the exact SANs you need.
- Terraform: we have a small module (rdw-private-dns) we can share; it provisions the CNAMEs and the ALB listener rules.

I'll drop the Terraform snippets and the module link in the follow-up doc. Laura, can you confirm compliance artifacts we need if Acme wants Redwood-managed certs?

— Markus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Soojin / Markus — thanks, that is very helpful. Short answers below:
- We prefer Option B (Redwood-managed termination) because we want better observability and the ability to use Redwood features (structured logging, tracing).
- Vault is the source of truth for cert issuance. We can either:
  1) Provide Redwood a Vault role with limited issue/renew permissions (scoped to a specific PKI path), or
  2) Agree to a workflow where Acme pushes PEM bundles to an S3 bucket that Redwood fetches after encryption/rotation.
- Our security team requires that private keys never be exported from our HSM. If Redwood needs to handle keys, we want a key-wrap integration so keys are generated ephemeral and wrapped by our HSM.
- We want mTLS enabled for control-plane endpoints (admin APIs). Data-plane will be optional.

We attached the SOW scope PDF with a callout for certificate responsibilities. Also, can Redwood provide an audit checklist (what logs/events you emit) and a short runbook for certificate rotation?

Alice
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme

Alice — great, thanks for the decision and the options. Quick summary / next steps so procurement and security have an action list:

1) Redwood will operate termination inside your VPC (Option B) with the following constraints:
   - Integration model: we will use Vault PKI API with a scoped machine user. Required: role name and endpoint + ephemeral token exchange method.
   - Key custody: we will generate ephemeral keys and call your key-wrap API so private keys are wrapped in your HSM. Redwood never stores unwrapped private keys.

2) mTLS: enable for control-plane APIs. We'll provide client cert validation and a simple rotation job. We will accept your CA chain for validation.

3) DNS: Acme infra will create private hosted zone and CNAMEs point to rdp-acme-prod.redwood-internal (we will give canonical names + Terraform snippets).

4) Compliance / Audit: Laura (cc) will provide the checklist items we can emit: cert issue/renew events, rotation timestamps, integration logs to your SIEM, and a short runbook for emergency rotation.

5) Deliverables and timeline:
   - Draft Terraform + ALB listener rules (Redwood) — by 2026-04-06
   - Vault integration runbook (Redwood) — by 2026-04-07
   - Compliance checklist & SIEM mapping (Redwood/Laura) — by 2026-04-05

6) SOW / procurement: we've shared a draft SOW link (DocuSign) for signatures. Once signed we'll schedule a 60-minute onboarding call to do the handshake and in-VPC tests.

Action items:
- Alice: confirm Vault role name and whether your team prefers the scoped role or S3 push model by EOD Mon 2026-04-05.
